Subject: OpalBridge SIG / SOC2 RFI - initial ask and timeline

Hi Kimberly / Priyom,

Thanks again for the quick intro call yesterday. Attaching our SIG+SOC2 workbook (OpalBridge_SIG_Questionnaire_20261128.xlsx) — we flagged ~45 items we want substantiated prior to contract execution. Top priorities for procurement: cryptographic key custody proof, telemetry retention/sample logs, and proof of SOC2 control operation for access reviews.

Target: vendor responses and artifacts by 14 Dec so our legal/procurement can finalize the PO. Could you confirm:
- a single staging manifest that lists each control, owner, artifact filename and estimated delivery date?
- who on your side will be the day-to-day contact for evidence collection and exceptions?

Appreciate a quick confirm and proposed cadence (we can do 30m weekly).

Thanks,
Sally Park
Head of Vendor Risk — OpalBridge

Subject: Re: OpalBridge SIG / SOC2 RFI - initial ask and timeline

Thanks Sally — we can meet the 14 Dec target with a coordinated sprint. Internal — putting owners on this thread so we have clear custody. Proposed plan:

1) Quick kickoff with OpalBridge this week (30m) to align on deliverables
2) Ship a single "staging manifest" CSV that maps each requested control to: Redwood control ID, artifact filename, owner, delivery date, and short substantiation note.
3) For controls that require operational evidence (telemetry, key rotation, access review snapshots), we will provide redacted examples and a provenance statement.

Owner suggestions: Priyom = primary evidence coordinator (collection + redaction), Jonas = telemetry/observability proofs (query samples + retention confirmation), Marcus = cryptographic/KMS proofs and architecture note. Kimberly = exec point and legal escalation.

Please review and confirm owners. I'll draft the manifest and circulate by EOD 2026-12-03 for your review.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: OpalBridge SIG / SOC2 RFI - telemetry samples and retention

Priyom / team — dropping telemetry guidance and sample query notes. Attached is a cleaned example of the queries and truncated output we'll provide (telemetry-query-samples.sql). Key points:

- We retain request traces (service-level logs with request/response metadata) for 90 days by default; aggregated metrics are kept 12 months.
- For the RFI we will supply three de-identified request-trace samples showing tokenization metadata, latency buckets, and route selection. Samples will be redacted to remove customer identifiers.
- The retention mechanism uses an automated lifecycle policy that moves raw traces to cold storage after 90 days; we will include the lifecycle policy snapshot as an artifact.

If OpalBridge needs longer retention for audit purposes we can propose a limited export agreement (note to legal).

-Jonas
Senior Observability Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: telemetry-query-samples.sql

Sally / OpalBridge team —

Thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Attached is our staging manifest (Redwood_OpalBridge_Artifact_Manifest_20261210.csv). The manifest maps each SIG/SOC2 control in your workbook to: Redwood control reference, artifact filename, owner, short substantiation note, and targeted delivery date. Highlights:

- KMS proof: Marcus included rotation history exports + role binding snapshots (redacted).
- Telemetry: Jonas provided three redacted trace samples and a lifecycle policy snapshot (retention = 90 days).
- Access reviews: quarterly snapshot files and JIRA crosswalk showing remediation actions.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm receipt and whether any controls need deeper artifacts (e.g., raw telemetry beyond the three samples).
2) If you want a recorded walkthrough of the manifest we can do a 45m session next week (I can host).
3) We'll push the final package to the Drive and HubSpot record by COB 2026-12-10 and remain on standby for clarifications.

Forwarding the manifest and selected artifacts to security@opalbridge.com.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
